[[File:Iwa-jinja (Matsumoto) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]]
'''Iwa Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|伊和神社}}, ''Iwa-jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|松本市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumoto, Nagano|qq=}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture|1=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. It is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=}}. Its modern status is a former {{ill|Village Shrine|en|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}}. The official name is "Iwa-sha," but it is commonly referred to as "Iwa Shrine."<ref>[http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/syouenchiku.htm 松塩筑支部] (Nagano Prefecture Shrine Bureau).</ref> 
=== Deities ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)<ref>[http://www.genbu.net/data/sinano/iwa_title.htm 伊和神社] (Genbuko personal website).</ref>
=== History ===
In ancient times, {{ill|provincial governors|en|国司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/provincial governors|qq=}} visited all shrines in their provinces, starting from the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}}. To facilitate this, a {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} was established near the provincial capital to enshrine the gods collectively for easier rituals. Iwa Shrine is presumed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Province|qq=}}. 
The provincial capital was initially located near {{ill|Ueda, Nagano|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda, Nagano|qq=}}, but it is believed to have moved to {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsumoto, Nagano|qq=}} in the early Heian period.<ref>"Shinano Province" in {{Cite book|title=Nagano Prefecture Place names|editor=平凡社}}.</ref> The area around the shrine has been called "Sōja" since ancient times, indicating the presence of a {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} and possibly the provincial capital.<ref name="説明板">Shrine grounds information board.</ref>
The name "Iwa" may derive from the nearby shrine "In'yaku-sha," which enshrined the official seal and key of the provincial storehouse. A theory suggests "In" (seal) transformed into "I," and "Yaku" (key) became "Wa" through scribal errors.<ref name="説明板"/> Another theory posits that the shrine enshrines the deity {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}, known as Iwa Myōjin, brought from the {{ill|Iwa Shrine (Hyōgo)|en|伊和神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwa Shrine (Hyōgo)|qq=}} in {{ill|Harima Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Harima Province|qq=}}.<ref name="説明板"/> The "Shinpū Tōki" (Edo period) mentions a local official, Satsuma-no-Kami, inviting Iwa Myōjin from Harima Province to create "Sōja Rokusha Daimyōjin," though this is considered a misinterpretation of earlier records.<ref name="地名">"Sōja Village" in ''Nagano Prefecture Place names''.</ref>
In the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Village Shrine|en|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}} under the modern shrine classification system and listed as a {{ill|Kensaihei Shrine|en|神饌幣帛料供進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensaihei Shrine|qq=}}.<ref>Shrine stone monument.</ref>
== Sub-Shrines ==
* **Kokage Shrine** – Dedicated to silkworm cultivation, built during the height of the local silk industry.
* **Sōja Iwa Daimyōjin** – Five shrines representing:
** {{ill|Usui Sadamitsu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Usui Sadamitsu|qq=}}
** {{ill|Sakata no Kintoki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakata no Kintoki|qq=}}
** {{ill|Minamoto no Yorimitsu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamoto no Yorimitsu|qq=}}
** {{ill|Watanabe no Tsuna|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watanabe no Tsuna|qq=}}
** {{ill|Urabe no Suetake|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Urabe no Suetake|qq=}}
=== Grounds ===
The shrine grounds feature numerous ancient {{ill|Zelkova serrata|en|ケヤキ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zelkova serrata|qq=}} trees. Two prominent zelkova trees at the entrance were formerly designated as a prefectural Natural Monument and are now protected as a city-level Natural Monument due to their age and declining health.<ref name="松本市">[http://takara.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/city/158.html 伊和神社のケヤキ群] (Matsumoto City Cultural Property website).</ref>
